title: rejects_all_zero_x25519_shared_secret: early error paths bypass poison()
description:
Root Cause: The test constructs a message_2 with 33 bytes in the bstr (32-byte G_Y + 1-byte ciphertext) but no C_R identifier at the end. When begin_process_message_2 calls parse_identifier(&msg2[consumed..]) at line 270 on the empty remainder, parse_identifier returns Err(EdhocError::InvalidMessage) because the slice is empty. The ? operator propagates this error and returns early WITHOUT calling self.poison().

The bug is that lines 269-272 and 279 have early error returns that bypass the poison() call at lines 339-341, which only handles errors from the closure at lines 287-337.

Affected Test: rejects_all_zero_x25519_shared_secret

Location: /Volumes/Attic/Desktop/Projects/crates/oscore/src/edhoc/initiator.rs:270

Suggested Fix: Move the early parsing logic (lines 269-286 in initiator.rs) inside the closure that already has proper error handling at lines 287-337. This ensures all error paths go through the if result.is_err() { self.poison(); } handler at lines 339-341. Alternatively, wrap lines 269-286 in a separate Result block that explicitly calls self.poison() before returning errors.

Error Type: Missing poison() call on early error paths - security-relevant: failed handshakes should wipe secrets and poison state to prevent reuse
